# `js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links`

**One form for labelled links in @see tags**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `enable_fixer` |
| **Fix** | `auto` — `codelaw fix` applies it; it never changes what the code does |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-jsdoc/normalize-see-links` |

## What it checks

A labelled link in a `@see` tag is written `{@link target|label}`: a Markdown link `[label](target)` and a prefix link `[label]{@link target}` are rewritten to it (the plugin's default `canonicalForm: "pipe"`). A link that cannot be rewritten safely — one written `{@link target label}`, a Markdown link inside a code span, one to a scoped package (`@scope/pkg`), one with an empty label, or text that looks like a link and is not — is reported as `@see link cannot be safely normalized.`, with no fix. Targets are percent-encoded where `|`, `{` or `}` would end the link. The `canonicalForm: "prefix"` and `wrapBareUrls` options are not built.

**Why:** Documentation tools read `{@link}`, not Markdown, in a `@see`; a mix of forms means some links come out as plain text.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:js/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/recommended"]

[rules]
"js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enable_fixer` | `boolean` | `true` | offer the rewrite |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links"]
severity = "error"

[rules."js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links".options]
enable_fixer = true
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links" = { severity = "error", options = { enable_fixer = false } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `enable_fixer`

*boolean* · default `true`

offer the rewrite

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links".options]
enable_fixer = false
```

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links" = { options = { enable_fixer = false } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links" = { severity = "warn", options = { enable_fixer = false } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"enable_fixer": false}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/jsdoc-normalize-see-links  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Write the link as `{@link target|label}` (the fix does).

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
/**
 * @see [the docs](https://example.com/docs)
 */
function f() {}
```

#### Do

```js
/**
 * @see {@link https://example.com/docs|the docs}
 */
function f() {}
```

#### Fixed

```js
/**
 * @see {@link https://example.com/docs|the docs}
 */
function f() {}
```
